message.text: I should look through the codebase to see if there's any rate limiting middleware already implemented.
I'm not finding any matches, so let me check the go.mod file to see if there are any rate limiting libraries available, like golang.org/x/time/rate.

No rate-limiting dependency or code exists at all.

r02.

**Premise correction:** There is no per-user API rate-limiting middleware in this repository. I searched the entire Go source tree for "ratelimit", "rate_limit", "rate-limit", "throttle", and "limiter" (case-insensitive) and found zero matches, and `go.mod` contains no rate-limiting library (e.g. `golang.org/x/time/rate` or similar) as a dependency.

There is a `maxConcurrentThumbnails`/`semaphore.Weighted` concurrency cap in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:46,107,448-451` (`internal-thumbnailSemaphore`), but that limits concurrent thumbnail *generation* work to prevent memory exhaustion — it is not a per-user request-rate limiter and applies globally across all users, not per-user quotas. Beyond that, I could not find any middleware, interceptor, or handler wrapper anywhere in `server/` that tracks or caps request counts per user/IP over time.

So the premise of the question doesn't hold for this codebase — there's nothing to cite as "the per-user API rate-limiting middleware" because it doesn't exist here.
